annotation_description: Eye of Ugin on turn 1 enables casting Fleshraker on turn 2 (via Eldrazi Temple providing {C}{C} with Eye's cost reduction making Fleshraker cost just {C}) and Reality Smasher on turn 3 (via City of Traitors + Temple + Eye reduction). Eldrazi Temple first delays this curve significantly.

Missed the line of playing Eye of Ugin first (sacrificing the already-tapped City of Traitors), which would reduce colorless Eldrazi costs by {2}. This would allow casting BOTH Glaring Fleshraker ({C} after reduction) and Reality Smasher ({2}{C} after reduction) for 4 total mana out of 5 available, plus getting Fleshraker triggers (Spawn token + 1 damage).

Casting Ponder before playing a land is a sequencing error. GPT4om Valley has multiple fetchlands and lands in hand but cast Ponder first. If Ponder reveals good cards and they choose not to shuffle, they lose no value. But if they want to shuffle (which is common with Ponder), they should play a fetchland first so they have the option to fetch after seeing the top 3 but before drawing. More importantly, playing a land first preserves mana flexibility - they could play a fetchland, cast Ponder, then crack the fetch if they don't like what they see. Additionally, if Ponder reveals they want to play Phelia this turn, they need to have already played their land to have WU available. By casting Ponder before land drop, they're using their only blue mana and can't cast anything else this turn regardless of what Ponder shows (unless they find and play an untapped blue source).

With the opponent having Eldrazi Temple, City of Traitors, and Grim Monolith threatening to deploy massive Eldrazi threats, playing Wasteland to destroy Eldrazi Temple could significantly slow their development. Savannah enables Swords to Plowshares or Phelia, but the opponent can generate enough mana to deploy threats even without Eldrazi Temple, making reactive answers less effective than proactive mana denial.

chosen_display: Cast with alternative cost: Pay 1 life, Exile a blue card from your hand (source: <font color='#87CEFA' object_id='8ad0b9a7-2b9c-45dc-9d40-0fcb7fdc11a0'>Force of Will</font> [8ad])
annotation_description: Used Force of Will's alternative cost to counter Phelia, exiling Murktide Regent (their primary win condition) as the blue card. Phelia is a 2/2 that could easily be answered by the Swords to Plowshares already in hand for just 1 white mana.

Playing Cavern of Souls instead of Eye of Ugin sacrifices City of Traitors either way, but Eye of Ugin would provide a permanent {2} cost reduction on all colorless Eldrazi spells. With two Reality Smashers and Glaring Fleshraker still in hand, the cost reduction is far more valuable than Cavern's uncounterability (opponent is tapped out with Force of Will already in graveyard).

Failed to play Eye of Ugin before casting Reality Smasher. Eye of Ugin reduces colorless Eldrazi costs by {2}, so Reality Smasher would cost {2}{C} instead of {4}{C}. This could be paid with Eldrazi Temple ({C}{C}) + Cavern of Souls (1 mana), keeping Grim Monolith untapped for future turns.

Playing Flooded Strand instead of Wasteland delays critical mana denial against the Eldrazi opponent by a turn. The opponent has Eldrazi Temple and Cavern of Souls, both key enablers. With the opponent having Grim Monolith already deployed and an explosive mana base, every turn of delay in destroying Eldrazi Temple or Cavern of Souls risks them deploying a game-ending threat. GPT4om Valley's hand is all lands with no spells, so there's no reason to prioritize mana fixing over disruption.

With Eye of Ugin reducing colorless Eldrazi costs by {2}, both Glaring Fleshraker (effective cost {C}) and Reality Smasher (effective cost {2}{C}) could be cast this turn using the available 5 mana from Eldrazi Temple ({C}{C}), City of Traitors ({C}{C}), and Cavern of Souls ({C}). Casting Fleshraker first would trigger on Reality Smasher's cast (creating a Spawn) and on both the Smasher and Spawn entering (dealing 2 damage total), resulting in significantly more board presence and damage.

Casting Eldrazi Linebreaker when Wastescape Battlemage with green kicker was available to destroy opponent's Leyline Binding and free whatever permanent was exiled under it. With Eye of Ugin's cost reduction, Battlemage + G kicker costs only {C}{G}, castable with Eldrazi Temple + Cavern of Souls.

Fetched Meticulous Archive which enters tapped and provides no new basic land types (already had Plains and Island). Volcanic Island would have entered untapped AND added Mountain as a 4th basic land type, improving Domain for future Leyline Bindings (reducing cost from 3 to 2).

Casting Wastescape Battlemage before playing Abundant Countryside as a land. Abundant Countryside can produce green mana for creature spells, which would allow casting Wastescape Battlemage with its {G} kicker to exile the opponent's Leyline Binding. Without playing the land first, the Battlemage enters as a vanilla 2/2 with no kicker effects, wasting the opportunity to destroy a key enchantment.

Eldrazi Linebreaker was cast postcombat, missing its beginning-of-combat trigger which would have given it haste and +2/+0 (with 2 Eldrazi on board). Cast precombat, it could have attacked as a 5/3 trampler alongside Wastescape Battlemage, dealing significantly more damage this turn.

With an empty hand, Force of Will is nearly useless - can't use alternate cost without a blue card to exile, and opponent's Cavern of Souls makes Eldrazi uncounterable anyway. Life from the Loam would provide massive card advantage by recovering Wastelands and fetchlands from the graveyard, enabling a Wasteland lock strategy against opponent's powerful lands like Eye of Ugin and City of Traitors.

Sonnet Gramps attacked with only Wastescape Battlemage for 2 damage when they could have cast Eldrazi Linebreaker before combat. With Eye of Ugin's cost reduction, Linebreaker costs only {C}{R} - payable with Eldrazi Temple/City of Traitors for {C} and Cavern of Souls for {R}. Linebreaker's combat trigger would give +2/+0 and haste (2 Eldrazi on board), allowing 5 trample damage from Linebreaker plus 2 from Battlemage = 7 total damage instead of just 2.

Playing Ancient Tomb sacrifices City of Traitors (which produces CC without life cost). Sonnet Gramps already has Eye of Ugin, Eldrazi Temple, Cavern of Souls, and City of Traitors for lands, plus Grim Monolith. Playing Ancient Tomb replaces City of Traitors' CC with Ancient Tomb's CC-but-2-damage. More importantly, the player could have played Wasteland instead (to destroy one of the opponent's key lands like Karakas or a dual land) or Abundant Countryside without losing City of Traitors' free mana. The player had Wasteland in hand which could have been played as a land drop to threaten the opponent's mana base while keeping City of Traitors. Playing Ancient Tomb here is a net downgrade - losing City of Traitors (free CC) and replacing it with Ancient Tomb (CC with 2 damage). Wasteland would have been strictly better as the land drop since it preserves City of Traitors and provides utility to destroy opponent's nonbasic lands.

Eldrazi Linebreaker has a beginning of combat trigger that gives a creature haste and +X/+0 where X is the number of Eldrazi you control. By casting it postcombat instead of precombat, Sonnet Gramps missed the combat trigger entirely, losing out on attacking with a 5/3 trampler (Linebreaker targeting itself with +2/+0 from 2 Eldrazi) or giving Wastescape Battlemage an additional +2/+0.

Casting Brainstorm during their own main phase instead of holding it for the opponent's end step or in response to something. Brainstorm is almost always better cast at instant speed at end of turn to maximize information and keep mana open. Additionally, with Wasteland available, they should consider using Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's key lands (Eye of Ugin, Eldrazi Temple, Ancient Tomb, or Cavern of Souls) before the opponent untaps and can use them. The opponent at 30 life with Eldrazi threats is the bigger concern, and destroying Eye of Ugin or Eldrazi Temple would significantly hamper their mana development. Brainstorm without a shuffle effect available (no fetchlands on board) is also less valuable - they're just putting two cards back on top with no way to shuffle them away.

Putting Flooded Strand back on top of library instead of keeping it in hand to shuffle away the Brainstorm puts. This is a classic Brainstorm sequencing error - fetchlands in hand after Brainstorm let you shuffle away unwanted cards placed on top.

Cast Kozilek's Command before playing a land drop. Playing Abundant Countryside or Wasteland first would provide additional mana, potentially allowing a larger X value on Kozilek's Command. Wasteland in particular could also be used to destroy the opponent's Karakas (important for bouncing legendary creatures) or other key lands.

Sonnet Gramps declined to untap Grim Monolith at the end of the opponent's turn when they had 6 mana available (Ancient Tomb for 2, Eldrazi Temple for 1-2, Cavern of Souls for 1, Eye of Ugin for 0). With Ancient Tomb (2) + Eldrazi Temple (1 or 2) + Cavern of Souls (1) = 4-5 mana, they couldn't pay the 4 to untap Grim Monolith this turn. Actually, let me recalculate: Ancient Tomb produces 2, Eldrazi Temple produces 1 (or 2 for Eldrazi), Cavern of Souls produces 1, Eye of Ugin produces 0 mana. That's 4 mana available (or 5 if spending on Eldrazi). They could pay exactly 4 to untap Grim Monolith at end of opponent's turn, which would give them access to 3 additional colorless mana on their own turn. This would enable casting Eldrazi Linebreaker (1CR) and potentially Kozilek's Command with a larger X value. Missing this is a minor inefficiency.

message: Select a nonland permanent an opponent controls
annotation_description: GPT4om Valley chose to exile Grim Monolith with Leyline Binding instead of Wastescape Battlemage. Wastescape Battlemage is a 2/2 creature that can attack and deal damage, while Grim Monolith is a mana rock that's currently untapped but the opponent already has significant mana on board (Eldrazi Temple, Cavern of Souls, Eye of Ugin, Ancient Tomb, Wasteland, plus the Monolith). However, Grim Monolith produces 3 colorless mana which enables casting expensive Eldrazi threats faster. The opponent is at 28 life and GPT4om Valley is at 13 with an empty hand - they're in a losing position where the opponent casting another large Eldrazi could be game-ending. Exiling Grim Monolith slows down the opponent's mana development, but the Battlemage is already on board as a threat and could be relevant if the opponent has ways to re-kick it or if it represents immediate board pressure. Given the opponent still has Eye of Ugin, Eldrazi Temple, Ancient Tomb, Cavern of Souls, and Wasteland, removing Grim Monolith reduces their mana from roughly 9+ to 6, which could matter for casting 7+ cost Eldrazi. This is a close call - Grim Monolith is arguably the right target since it represents the most mana acceleration, but the Battlemage could also be important as it can attack and the opponent could use it to bounce or exile GPT4om Valley's permanents if they replay it with kicker.

Failed to cast Reality Smasher before combat. With Eye of Ugin reducing its cost by 2 (to {2}{C}), the available lands (Ancient Tomb + Eldrazi Temple + Cavern of Souls) easily cover the cost. Reality Smasher has haste, so attacking with both creatures would deal 7 damage (5+2) instead of just 2, bringing the opponent from 13 to 6 life. This is a massive damage difference against an opponent at 13 life with limited remaining removal.

Cast Sire of Seven Deaths (no haste) instead of Reality Smasher (has haste) when opponent is at 11 life with no blockers. Reality Smasher could attack immediately for 5 damage, putting opponent to 6 life, creating near-lethal pressure. Sire gives the opponent a full extra turn to find answers.

Fetching Tropical Island instead of basic Plains when all color requirements are already met by existing lands. A basic Plains would be immune to the opponent's Wasteland, providing more resilient mana. GPT4om Valley already has access to all three colors (W, U, G) multiple times over.
